entries.summary: No verified material directional change from the 21:54 EST assessment. Latest confirmed US cash closes remain Nasdaq -0.39%, SOX -0.54%, NVDA -4.34%, AMD +5.86% and AVGO +5.54% on November 12. New pre-PPI reporting gives an economist consensus of 6.6% year-on-year October producer inflation, a forecast, NOT the actual release. PPI is still pending at 08:30 EST November 13. Open Watch remains 159 events as of 2026-11-12T23:58:32+00:00. Synchronized overnight QQQ/SOX, rates, volatility, breadth and oil observations are unavailable.
bullish: Nasdaq closed -0.39% after opening -1.47%, showing substantial absorption of the initial Nvidia shock.
AMD +5.86% and AVGO +5.54% at Thursday's close indicate selective chip rotation rather than uniform sector capitulation.
Foxconn and Siemens data-center demand signals remain supportive of longer-run AI infrastructure spending; no attributable index response is established.

Applied Materials fiscal Q4 adjusted EPS $4.16 versus $4.06 expected and revenue $10.41B versus $10.3B; next-quarter guidance above estimates. Cisco reported adjusted EPS $1.40 versus $1.33 expected, revenue $18.5B versus $18.1B and raised outlook; positive AI networking demand evidence, not proof of Friday market response.
bearish: Nvidia closed -4.34% following the confirmed CEO transition, and SOX finished -0.54%; leadership and semiconductor benchmark remain vulnerable.
Higher oil and long yields reported earlier remain valuation risks, but current synchronized oil/yield measurements are missing.
Reuters reports at least a 25bp December Fed hike fully priced, with a 15% chance of a 50bp move; hotter PPI could worsen duration-sensitive equity pressure.
Applied Materials was reportedly nearly flat after hours despite its beat after falling 3.6% in regular trade; a strong report alone has not confirmed sector-wide risk appetite.

editorial.marketOverview: Thursday's Nasdaq -0.39%, SOX -0.54% and NVDA -4.34% closes still define the confirmed risk backdrop. AMD +5.86% and AVGO +5.54% signal chip-sector rotation, not uniform liquidation. Cisco and Applied Materials earnings strengthen the fundamental AI-infrastructure demand case but Friday's actual cash-market reaction has not occurred. No fresh synchronized overnight market snapshot supports a revised directional call.
editorial.whatChanged: A new pre-release market preview quotes a 6.6% year-over-year consensus for October PPI, due Friday at 08:30 EST. This is an expected value, not the release or a realized catalyst impact. The Open Watch event count and timestamp are unchanged, and no fresh synchronized market reaction has been established. The outlook therefore remains unchanged.
editorial.marketInterpretation: The bearish skew is driven by NVDA leadership fragility, still-negative SOX close and inflation/rates event risk. Strong AMD and AVGO performance, the recovery from Thursday's lows and positive infrastructure earnings temper conviction. PPI surprise and subsequent market behavior matter more than the headline consensus forecast alone.
editorial.threeDayPath: Friday November 13: compare the official PPI release to consensus, then examine matched 2Y/10Y yields, QQQ, SOX, NVDA, breadth and volatility after the open. Monday November 16: look for durable chip leadership and broad participation or renewed selling. Tuesday November 17: seek multi-session confirmation before changing regime. These are conditional scenarios rather than forecasts of precise prices.
editorial.bullCase: An at-or-below-consensus PPI, falling yields, stable NVDA, strong SOX relative performance and improving breadth could confirm that Thursday's shock was absorbed. AMD, AVGO, Cisco and Applied Materials offer constructive underlying evidence, but require a positive market response.
editorial.bearCase: An upside PPI surprise accompanied by rising yields, renewed NVDA/SOX losses, weak breadth and rising VXN/VIX could drive another QQQ leg lower. Elevated oil would intensify the inflation channel if verified contemporaneously; older oil quotes are not proof of current pressure.
editorial.watchNext: Check official BLS October PPI at 08:30 EST November 13, including revisions and consensus surprise. Obtain timestamp-matched QQQ/Nasdaq, SOX, NVDA/AMD/AVGO/AMAT/CSCO, 2Y/10Y, VXN/VIX, breadth, Brent/WTI and FedWatch; reassess Open Watch for genuinely new curated catalysts.
